proposed.explanation: The investor seeks long‑term growth with a 7+ year horizon and can tolerate medium risk. Using the evidence available up to the 2026‑11‑18 cutoff, Telecom Egypt (ETEL) shows the strongest net‑profit growth from 2024 to 2025: 22,578,063,000 EGP versus 10,111,328,000 EGP, a 123% increase. Its trailing twelve‑month basic/diluted EPS of 11.93 EGP yields a price‑to‑earnings ratio of about 11.9 (share price 141.95 EGP / 11.93 EGP), which is reasonable for a large‑cap telecom with solid earnings momentum. With 80,000 EGP cash the investor can purchase 563 ETEL shares at 141.95 EGP each, costing 79,918.85 EGP, leaving a small cash balance that respects the separate emergency‑fund rule. The decision is based solely on the reported net‑profit growth and P/E; other companies (COMI, EFID, TMGH) are not evaluated here. All figures are taken directly from the supplied evidence and expressed in base pounds.

claims.statement: ETEL net profit for year 2025 = 22,578,063,000 EGP
ETEL net profit for year 2024 = 10,111,328,000 EGP
ETEL basic/diluted EPS for year 2025 = 11.93 EGP

limitations: All figures are as printed in the reports up to the 2026‑11‑18 cutoff; no later data or market events are considered.
Net‑profit growth and P/E are based on trailing‑twelve‑month data only; future performance may differ.
The P/E calculation uses the stated EPS in base units (EGP) and the quoted share price; any mis‑reporting of units would affect the ratio.
The investor’s emergency‑fund requirement is assumed to be kept separate; the remaining cash after the purchase (≈11.15 EGP) is retained as cash.
No other financial metrics (dividend yield, balance‑sheet strength, macro‑economic factors) are evaluated here.
